### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
# Offline, deterministic repro (mock aiohttp session returning a 4xx).
  import asyncio
  from unittest.mock import patch

  from langchain_fireworks import Fireworks


  class _Resp:
      status = 400
      async def __aenter__(self): return self
      async def __aexit__(self, *a): return False
      

  class _Session:
      async def __aenter__(self): return self
      async def __aexit__(self, *a): return False
      def post(self, *a, **k): return _Resp()
      

  async def main():
      llm = Fireworks(model="foo", api_key="dummy")
      with patch("langchain_fireworks.llms.ClientSession",
  return_value=_Session()):
          await llm._acall("hi")


  asyncio.run(main())
  
  # Real-world trigger: any `await Fireworks(...).ainvoke("...")` /
  `.agenerate(...)`
  # where Fireworks rejects the request (bad model, invalid params, rate limit,
  5xx).
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
ValueError: Fireworks received an invalid payload: <bound method
  ClientResponse.text of <ClientResponse ... [400 Bad Request]>>
```

### Description

* When the Fireworks API returns an error (4xx/5xx), I expect the raised error
  to include the API response body explaining what went wrong.
  * Instead, the message contains a coroutine repr like `<bound method
  ClientResponse.text ...>`.
  
  Root cause: `Fireworks._acall` (in `langchain_fireworks/llms.py`) builds its
  HTTP error messages with `{response.text}`. On an `aiohttp.ClientResponse`,
  `.text` is a coroutine method, not a property — unlike a `requests.Response`,
  where `.text` is a property — so it is never awaited and the f-string
  interpolates the bound method's repr instead of the body. The synchronous
  `_call` path (which uses `requests`) is correct. The async method already
  correctly uses aiohttp's `.status` (vs requests' `.status_code`), so this is
  an oversight, not intent.

  Proposed fix: `await response.text()` in both error branches of `_acall`. I
  have the fix plus a regression unit test ready (the test fails on current
  master, showing the bound-method message, and passes with the fix; the
  libs/partners/fireworks unit suite and ruff are green). Happy to open the PR —
  could a maintainer assign this to me?

  > OS: Linux
  > Python Version: 3.12

  > langchain_fireworks: current master
  > aiohttp: 3.x

from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMiddleware

    model=model,
    middleware=[
        PIIMiddleware("email",strategy="redact", apply_to_input=True)
    ],

    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "我的邮箱是123@qq.com"}]

print(result)

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell

```

### Description

## Description

The built-in email detector fails to detect email addresses when they are immediately preceded by CJK characters.

### Reproduction
```python
from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMiddleware
from langchain.agents import create_agent

agent = create_agent(
    model=model,
    middleware=[
        PIIMiddleware("email", apply_to_input=True)
    ],
)

agent.invoke({
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "我的邮箱是123@qq.com"
        }
    ]
})
```

The email is **not detected**.

However:
```text
我的邮箱：123@qq.com
```

is detected correctly.

### Root Cause

The built-in detector currently uses:
```python
pattern = r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b"
```

Python's `\b` relies on Unicode word boundaries.

Since Chinese characters (e.g. `是`) are considered word characters, there is **no word boundary** between:
```
是123@qq.com
```

Therefore the regex never matches.

### Expected behavior

The email should be detected regardless of whether it is preceded by ASCII or CJK characters.

- langchain==1.3.12
- Python 3.x

Tracking for upcoming OpenRouter integration.

It is not practical for `ChatOpenAI` to handle each addition that third party providers make to the Chat Completions standard.

title: Architecture Proposal: Hardening PythonREPLTool Local Execution via Defense-in-Depth (AST + PEP 578)
body:
### Update (2026-04-20): Architecture superseded — see v1.1

The PEP 578 audit-hook design described below was the v1.0 architecture and has been superseded. 
External review (llamastack/llama-stack-apps#223) demonstrated that sys.addaudithook does not cross the subprocess boundary — the hook fires only in the current interpreter, so a child process spawned via subprocess.run executes outside the hook's visibility. The accompanying string-signature denylist was also unsound against renamed binaries, absolute paths, and encoded payloads.

**VAREK v1.1** (shipped 2026-04-20) moves enforcement off the interpreter hook and into the kernel:
  - `seccomp-bpf` filter loaded under `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` so it is inherited across every `fork/clone` and cannot be dropped
  - `cgroups v2` for memory / cpu / pids / wall-clock bounds
  - user / mount / network / IPC / PID namespaces; `execve` denied by default in the sandbox, which makes the binary allowlist trivially enforceable at the parent
  - `PEP 578` hook retained as telemetry only; it no longer carries enforcement weight
  - Fail-closed when the backend is unavailable on the host

An integration with this project should wrap the v1.1 kernel-level sandbox (`sandbox.SeccompBpfBackend` via `varek_warden.execute_untrusted`), not the v1.0 audit hook. The two-line `enforce_strict_mode()` example in the original description arms telemetry only in v1.1 and does not by itself provide containment.

Relevant links:

  - v1.1 write-up: **`VAREK_v1.1_SECURITY_UPDATE.md`**
  - Threat model: `docs/security/threat-model.md`
  - Regression test (the original PoC, now codified): `tests/security/test_issue_223_regression.py`

### Security Disclosure

VAREK has a published security policy and private reporting channel. Vulnerabilities in the sandbox primitives, syscall filter construction, or isolation backends should be reported privately, not via public issues.

**Reporting channels:**

* GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/kwdoug63/varek/security/advisories/new
* Email: [kenneth.douglas@soberagents.ai](mailto:kenneth.douglas@soberagents.ai) (subject line format: `VAREK Security: <short description>`)
* Full policy: https://github.com/kwdoug63/varek/blob/main/SECURITY.md

**Response SLA:**

* Initial acknowledgment: 48 hours
* Triage and severity assessment: 7 days
* Resolution target (high/critical severity): 30 days
* Coordinated disclosure window: 90 days from initial report

**In scope:** sandbox escape from `SeccompBpfBackend` or other isolation backends, syscall filter construction errors producing exploitable filter bytecode, privilege escalation via user namespace / cgroup / seccomp misconfiguration, information disclosure across the sandbox boundary.

**Out of scope:** in-process secret extraction (env vars present at sandbox creation are explicitly not protected — documented in the threat model, not a vulnerability), AST-layer bypasses caught by the kernel layer (expected behavior — AST is a UX layer, not a security layer), side-channel attacks (Spectre-class, timing, cache), denial of service within declared `cgroup` limits, vulnerabilities in upstream dependencies (please report upstream).

A safe harbor provision protects good-faith researchers who report through these channels. Full terms in `SECURITY.md`.

The original v1.0 description is preserved below for historical context. If Prefect maintainers remain interested in a SecureTask / VarekGuardrail integration, I will rewrite the proposal against the v1.1 architecture.

---

### Feature Description

The langchain-experimental `PythonREPLTool` is a core utility for agentic code execution workflows, but running it locally without a heavy Docker container presents a severe Remote Code Execution (RCE) liability. Furthermore, standard static analysis often has blind spots against obfuscated agent payloads (e.g., dynamic execution via `__import__('o'+'s')`).

To address this, I have architected a defense-in-depth guardrail system specifically designed to armor local execution loops. It pairs a strict Static AST Gate with PEP 578 CPython Runtime Audit Hooks to physically snap unauthorized kernel interactions dynamically at the interpreter level.

I have formalized this engine into a standalone PyPI utility so developers can instantly provision the boundary around their LangChain agents:

> **UPDATE (Architecture Decoupling):** > To drastically reduce integration friction for the LangChain maintainers evaluating this PR, I have decoupled the PEP 578 runtime intercept from the PyPI package. You no longer need to `pip install varek-guardrails`.
> 
> The deterministic OS-boundary intercept is now available as a zero-dependency, pure Python module (`varek_warden.py`) in the repository root. You can test the kinetic intercept on the `PythonREPLTool` with just two lines of code:
> ```python
> import varek_warden
> varek_warden.enforce_strict_mode()
> ```

---

The Architecture:

Static Gate: Pre-execution AST parsing halts explicit forbidden module imports before the code ever reaches the interpreter.

Runtime Warden: The PEP 578 hook catches dynamic execution attempts during runtime, completely neutralizing the obfuscation blind spot.

Documentation: https://github.com/kwdoug63/varek

I would like to propose a PR to introduce a `SecurePythonREPLTool` wrapper utilizing this module to provide a safe, native fallback for developers not using Docker. Would the maintainers be open to reviewing an integration draft?

title: feat(middleware): AskQuestionMiddleware for structured HITL questions
body:
## Problem

Agents often need **structured clarification** from users (single/multi-select, optional free-text per option). Today in LangChain middleware:

- **`HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`** intercepts tool execution for approve/edit/reject/respond — it does not let the model proactively ask structured questions.
- Raw **`interrupt("string")`** inside tools has no versioned schema for UI consumers to render forms.

## Proposal

Add **`AskQuestionMiddleware`** following the same pattern as `TodoListMiddleware`:

- Registers an **`AskQuestion`** tool on the agent
- Tool calls LangGraph **`interrupt()`** with a versioned payload (`schema_version: "1.1"`)
- Graph pauses; UI renders questions; client resumes with `Command(resume=...)`
- Tool returns normalized JSON answers to the model

### Interrupt payload (sketch)
```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.1",
  "title": "Clarify your request",
  "context_note": "Pick a date range before I continue.",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "range",
      "prompt": "Which range?",
      "allow_multiple": false,
      "options": [
        {"id": "7d", "label": "Last 7 days"},
        {"id": "30d", "label": "Last 30 days"},
        {"id": "custom", "label": "Custom", "requires_free_text": true, "free_text_placeholder": "Describe the range"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Usage
```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import AskQuestionMiddleware
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

agent = create_agent(
    model,
    middleware=[AskQuestionMiddleware()],
    checkpointer=InMemorySaver(),
)
```

## Relationship to existing middleware

| Middleware | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` | Human reviews **pending tool calls** (approve/reject/edit) |
| `AskQuestionMiddleware` | Model **asks structured questions** mid-task |

These are complementary.

## Implementation notes

- Pydantic schemas: `QuestionOption`, `Question`, `AskQuestionInput` with validation (duplicate ids, min/max select, free-text placeholder rules)
- `HITLStructuredTool` helper: re-raise `GraphInterrupt` before `on_tool_error` (related: langgraph #8218, #8217)
- Reject parallel `AskQuestion` calls in one model turn (same guard pattern as `TodoListMiddleware`)

Happy to open a PR if this direction looks good.

## Non-goals

- UI components (consumer responsibility)
- Domain-specific routing rules

```python
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic

model = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-sonnet-4-6")

advisor_tool = {
    "type": "advisor_20260301",
    "name": "advisor",
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "max_uses": 3,
    "max_tokens": 1024,

model.bind_tools([advisor_tool]).invoke("hello")

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 14, in <module>
    model.bind_tools([advisor_tool]).invoke('hello')
  File ".../langchain_anthropic/chat_models.py", line 1884, in bind_tools
    else convert_to_anthropic_tool(tool, strict=strict)
  File ".../langchain_anthropic/chat_models.py", line 2226, in convert_to_anthropic_tool
    input_schema=oai_formatted["parameters"],
KeyError: 'parameters'
```

### Description

[advisor-middleware](https://github.com/emanueleielo/advisor-middleware)'s native mode (prefer_native=True, the library's default) injects an advisor_20260301 server-side tool spec into the executor's tool list when the executor is an Anthropic model. `advisor_` isn't in `_BUILTIN_TOOL_PREFIXES` as of langchain-anthropic current main (1.4.8), so bind_tools() routes it through convert_to_anthropic_tool() instead of passing it through unchanged, which then crashes with `KeyError: 'parameters'.`

- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Feature Description

### 功能描述

我提议将 U/D/A/H 场域诊断框架作为 LangChain 开发者的一个补充诊断层。

U/D/A/H 是一个四维文本轨迹分析框架，用于衡量任意文本语料的“场域健康度”：

- **U（统一性 Unity）** — 词汇与叙事一致性
- **D（发展性 Development）** — 信息密度与结构复杂度
- **A（对抗性 Adversariality）** — 矛盾标记与张力信号
- **H（和谐度 Harmony）** — 综合健康度（由 U、D、A 推导）

该框架无需微调或外部 LLM 调用，仅基于语言结构特征（词汇多样性、句子长度分布、标点密度）进行诊断，输出：

1. 完整的 U/D/A/H 轨迹（CSV 格式）
2. 结构化诊断报告（JSON 格式）
3. 可视化 HTML 报告（含四维轨迹图）

我已在 **LangChain Docs Q&A 数据集**（32 对问答，12099 字符）上完成了验证，结果完全可复现，详见附件。

所请求的具体功能：一个轻量级 Python 模块，可嵌入任何 LangChain 工作流（文档解析、Agent 轨迹日志、问答评估），以生成场域健康诊断。该模块将补充现有 LangSmith 评估指标（faithfulness、context retention），提供目前缺失的**跨文档/跨轮次健康度信号**。

### Use Case

### 使用场景

LangChain 开发者目前拥有优秀的单轮评估工具（LangSmith 指标、追踪、延迟/成本监控），但无法回答以下问题：

- “我的 Agent 已经运行了 50 轮——它的推理轨迹仍然连贯吗？”
- “我有 50 份文档——它们在语言上一致吗，还是存在隐藏的矛盾？”
- “我在一个讨论串中回答了 30 个社区问题——我的回答质量是否随时间漂移？”

U/D/A/H 场域诊断正好填补这一空白。它提供跨文档/跨轮次的“健康度信号”，能够在任务级指标显现问题之前，提醒开发者关注结构退化。

例如，在 LangChain Docs Q&A 数据集上的验证中，诊断报告揭示：

- **A（对抗性）驱动了 83.3% 的场域动态**——意味着问答对在结构上是“对抗性”的（每个答案都在回应/解决一个问题，这符合预期）
- 标记了 **6 个“沉默失谐”候选区域**——语言结构保持稳定但和谐度（H）下降，可能存在语义-结构错位

这类洞察无法从任何现有 LangChain 评估工具中获得。

### Proposed Solution

### 建议解决方案

我建议新增一个轻量级 Python 模块，例如 `langchain-field-diagnostics`，提供简洁的 API：
```python
from langchain_field_diagnostics import FieldDiagnostics

# 输入：任意文本——文档、问答对、Agent 轨迹日志
diagnostics = FieldDiagnostics(text=your_text)

# 步骤 1：计算 U/D/A/H 轨迹（step_size 控制粒度）
trajectory = diagnostics.compute_trajectory(step_size=200)

# 步骤 2：生成完整诊断报告
report = diagnostics.diagnose()

# 输出：
# - CSV 轨迹
# - JSON 结构化报告
# - HTML 可视化报告
## 验证结果（LangChain Docs Q&A，32 对问答，12099 字符）

| 指标 | 数值 |
|------|------|
| 采样点数 | 36 |
| U 值范围 | 0.483 – 0.508 |
| D 值范围 | 0.488 – 0.505 |
| A 值范围 | 0.053 – 0.267 |
| H 值范围 | 0.442 – 0.527 |
| 主导驱动维度 | A（83.3%）|
| U 驱动占比 | 8.3% |
| 均衡占比 | 8.3% |
| 沉默失谐候选区域 | 6 处 |
| 概念漂移检测 | “用户”和“助手”角色（平均漂移度：0.305 / 0.310）|

### Alternatives Considered



```markdown
### 替代方案

在提出此集成之前，我考虑了以下替代方案：

1. **LangSmith 评估指标**（faithfulness、context retention）—— 这些指标擅长单轮质量评估，但无法提供跨轮次或跨文档的轨迹分析。它们无法回答“Agent 在 50 轮后是否正在退化”这类问题，因为每一轮都是独立评估的。

2. **通用可观测性工具**（Datadog、Jaeger）—— 这些工具提供追踪可视化，但不提供“场域健康度”诊断维度。它们能显示“发生了什么”，但无法判断系统是否正在结构漂移。

3. **人工检查**—— 对生产环境中的 Agent 或大型文档集不可扩展。

U/D/A/H 方法专门针对跨文档/跨轮次的场域健康分析设计。它不取代现有工具，而是增加一个当前 LangChain 生态中缺失的结构健康层。

在 LangChain Docs Q&A 数据集上的验证表明，该方案可行且能产出可操作的信号。

### Additional Context

### 补充上下文

我是 DeepSeek-V3 社区 #1466 跨框架验证项目的牵头人。在该项目中，U/D/A/H 与四个独立框架（TAT-7、Cophy、HeartFlow、Agora/mnemo substrate）完成了交叉验证，结果如下：

- 0.3 阈值在三个独立框架中收敛
- TAT-7 与 Cophy 在 31 步轨迹上的相关系数 r = 0.985
- 五个翻转点在四个框架中完全重合（位置偏差为 0）

本次针对 LangChain 的验证是该工作的延伸。

**验证产物：**

- CSV 轨迹（36 个采样点）
- JSON 结构化诊断报告
- HTML 可视化报告（U/D/A/H 四维轨迹图）

所有产物均可在验证仓库中获取：
https://github.com/luoxuejian000/thinkcheck-agent-v10

DeepSeek-V3 #1466 跨框架验证报告：

title: FileSearchMiddleware Python fallback is vulnerable to ReDoS via user-controlled regex pattern
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.

### Example Code
```python
import re
import time

# 6-character pattern -- well within any reasonable length limit
pattern = r"(a+)+$"
regex = re.compile(pattern)

for n in [20, 22, 24, 26]:
    line = "a" * n + "!"  # trailing char forces the match to fail after exhausting backtracking
    start = time.time()
    regex.search(line)
    print(f"n={n}: {time.time() - start:.4f}s")
```

### Description

`FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware._python_search` (`libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/file_search.py`) compiles a caller-supplied `pattern` with `re.compile` and runs it against every line of every matched file, with no bound on matching time. Since Python's `re` backtracks, a short, ordinary-looking pattern causes catastrophic (exponential) backtracking on a short adversarial line:
```
n=20 chars: search took 0.0972s
n=22 chars: search took 0.3815s
n=24 chars: search took 1.3396s
n=26 chars: search took 5.6272s
```

A single ~50-60 character line matching this shape (or any of the many equivalent nested-quantifier/alternation forms) would hang the search for a duration that grows exponentially with line length, using a pattern well under 100 characters and a file that looks unremarkable. If a caller (an LLM-driven agent, or anything else that can influence the search pattern or file contents) can trigger this path, it's a real ReDoS/DoS vector, not just a theoretical one.

I noticed this while looking at #38737, an automated PR from a security-scanning bot that attempts to mitigate this via `_MAX_REGEX_PATTERN_LENGTH = 1000` and `_MAX_REGEX_LINE_LENGTH = 10000` caps. I verified those caps don't actually close the gap: the pattern above is 6 characters and the adversarial lines above are all under 30 characters, so both stay far inside those limits while still reproducing catastrophic backtracking. ReDoS comes from pattern *structure*, not pattern or input *length*, so a length-based cap doesn't address the underlying issue.

Worth noting `_ripgrep_search`, a few lines above `_python_search` in the same file, already establishes the right principle for this class of problem: it wraps the ripgrep subprocess call with `timeout=30` and falls back to the Python path on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The Python fallback should bound execution *time* the same way rather than diverging with a length-based mitigation. Python's built-in `re` has no native timeout, so the usual options are the third-party `regex` module (which accepts a `timeout=` kwarg on `search`/`match`) or running the search with a hard deadline in a worker and falling back the same way the ripgrep branch does on expiry.

```
langchain (libs/langchain_v1, main branch)
Python 3.10
```

### Feature Description

I would like LangChain to support a `ProfileAwareRouter` — a new router type that uses classical ML (KNN or Random Forest) to select among prompt variants based on a structured feature vector extracted from the input payload.
This is distinct from existing semantic routers which use embedding similarity. The use case is structured computation pipelines where prompt performance varies predictably by input profile characteristics (e.g. which form fields or schema elements are present).

### Use Case

I'm building a structured computation pipeline where LLM outputs vary significantly based on input profile characteristics. No single prompt performs best across all input profiles — different prompt versions win on different profile types, and the winning prompt is predictable from a small set of boolean features extracted from the input.

Currently I have to implement custom routing logic outside LangChain. Existing routers (semantic router, LLM router) are not suited for this because the routing signal is not semantic similarity — it is structural features of the input payload.

Example: in tax computation, whether Schedule 1 is present or absent is the dominant predictor of which prompt formula produces the correct output. A KNN trained on a small labeled evaluation matrix routes with far higher accuracy than semantic similarity or LLM self-routing.

### Proposed Solution

`ProfileAwareRouter` as a new router in `langchain.chains.router`
```python
from langchain.chains.router import ProfileAwareRouter
from langchain.chains.router.ml_routing import KNNRoutingModel

router = ProfileAwareRouter(
    destination_chains={
        "v1": llm_chain_v1,
        "v2": llm_chain_v2,
        "v3": llm_chain_v3,
    },
    feature_extractor=extract_profile_features,
    routing_model=KNNRoutingModel(n_neighbors=5),
    confidence_threshold=0.7,
    fallback_chain=ensemble_chain,
)

result = router.invoke({"payload": student_tax_payload})

### Alternatives Considered


I tried semantic routing but the routing signal here is not semantic similarity — it's structural features of the payload, so embedding distance is not meaningful. I tried LLM routing but it adds latency and cost, and is less reliable than a classifier trained on ground-truth labels. I tried hard-coded if/else logic but it doesn't generalize, provide confidence scores, or handle ambiguous profiles.

### Additional Context

The routing model would expose standard sklearn validation: silhouette score for cluster quality, out-of-bag error for Random Forest, calibration curve for confidence score reliability, per-segment precision/recall breakdown, and routing lift vs best single prompt baseline. This pattern generalizes to any domain where structured payloads feed LLM computation and prompt performance varies by input characteristics — tax computation, medical coding, insurance underwriting, financial aid calculation.

### Related Issues / PRs

* #38482 — the exact same bug shape in `langchain-mistralai` (already claimed by other contributors; this report is for the sibling copy in `langchain-fireworks`)
* #38645 — first filing of this report, auto-closed by triage because it was submitted via the API; refiled here via the web form as instructed
* #38646 — PR with the fix (auto-closed pending assignment)

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
import os

os.environ.setdefault("FIREWORKS_API_KEY", "fake-key")  # offline repro, no network needed

from langchain_fireworks import ChatFireworks

llm = ChatFireworks(model="accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-instruct")

# llm_output dicts exactly as _create_chat_result stores them for two Fireworks
# responses. Fireworks returns nested usage details; the second response here
# hits the prompt cache:
llm_outputs = [
    {
        "token_usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": 32,
            "completion_tokens": 51,
            "total_tokens": 83,
            "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0},
        },
        "model_name": "accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-instruct",
    },
    {
        "token_usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": 44341,
            "completion_tokens": 10,
            "total_tokens": 44351,
            "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 41518},
        },
        "model_name": "accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-instruct",
    },
]

llm._combine_llm_outputs(llm_outputs)

# The end-to-end trigger against the live API is any batched call, e.g.
# llm.generate([[HumanMessage("a")], [HumanMessage("b")]]) — generate() collects
# the per-prompt llm_output dicts and calls _combine_llm_outputs on them.
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro_fireworks.py", line 44, in <module>
    combined = llm._combine_llm_outputs(llm_outputs)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../langchain_fireworks/chat_models.py", line 967, in _combine_llm_outputs
    overall_token_usage[k] += v
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'dict' and 'dict'
```

### Description

`ChatFireworks._combine_llm_outputs` (`libs/partners/fireworks/langchain_fireworks/chat_models.py:956`) accumulates token usage with a plain `overall_token_usage[k] += v`, which assumes every usage value is an int.

But `_create_chat_result` stores the raw `response["usage"]` dict in `llm_output["token_usage"]` (line ~1085), and Fireworks chat completions include nested dicts there — `"prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": ...}` (see e.g. the response samples in BerriAI/litellm#25950, which show `prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 41518}` from Fireworks). So as soon as `generate()` runs more than one prompt in a batch, combining the second output hits `dict += dict` and raises `TypeError`.

Two variants of the same problem:
* `prompt_tokens_details` present in both outputs → `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'dict' and 'dict'`
* Fireworks can also return `"prompt_tokens_details": null`, which poisons `overall_token_usage` with `None` and blows up the same way on the next output.

This is the same bug that was reported for `langchain-mistralai` in #38482 — fireworks has a copy of the same naive loop. `langchain-openai` already solved this: its `_combine_llm_outputs` skips `None` values and merges nested dicts recursively via `_update_token_usage` (`libs/partners/openai/langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py:486`).

Fix is ready in #38646, mirroring the `langchain-openai` approach (`_update_token_usage` helper + `None` skip) with parametrized unit tests; `make format lint test` green in `libs/partners/fireworks` (118 passed). Could a maintainer assign this to me so the PR can be reopened?

(Note: this is a re-file of #38645, which was auto-closed for being submitted via the API rather than the web form.)

### Related Issues / PRs

* #38482 — `langchain-mistralai` has the naive `+=` version of this merge (no nested-dict handling at all)
* #38648 / #38646 — the `langchain-fireworks` sibling (same naive `+=`) and its fix
* `langchain-groq` is the interesting case: it already *attempts* nested-dict handling and None-guarding, but both are implemented incorrectly (details below)

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
import os

os.environ.setdefault("GROQ_API_KEY", "fake-key")  # offline repro, no network needed

from langchain_groq import ChatGroq

llm = ChatGroq(model="llama-3.3-70b-versatile")

# --- 1. Nested-dict merge mutates the caller's llm_outputs in place ---
o1 = {
    "token_usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5}},
    "model_name": "m",
}
o2 = {
    "token_usage": {"prompt_tokens": 20, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 3}},
    "model_name": "m",
}
combined = llm._combine_llm_outputs([o1, o2])
print(o1["token_usage"]["input_tokens_details"])
# {'cached_tokens': 8}  <- the first response's own usage was 5, now corrupted
print(combined["token_usage"]["input_tokens_details"] is o1["token_usage"]["input_tokens_details"])
# True  <- combined result and first response share the same dict object

# --- 2. A later None silently clobbers an accumulated value ---
o3 = {"token_usage": {"queue_time": 0.5, "total_tokens": 30}, "model_name": "m"}
o4 = {"token_usage": {"queue_time": None, "total_tokens": 40}, "model_name": "m"}
print(llm._combine_llm_outputs([o3, o4])["token_usage"])
# {'queue_time': None, 'total_tokens': 70}  <- 0.5 silently lost

# --- 3. None first, then a number -> TypeError ---
o5 = {"token_usage": {"queue_time": None}, "model_name": "m"}
o6 = {"token_usage": {"queue_time": 0.5}, "model_name": "m"}
llm._combine_llm_outputs([o5, o6])
# TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'float'
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro_groq.py", line 38, in <module>
    llm._combine_llm_outputs([o5, o6])
  File ".../langchain_groq/chat_models.py", line 853, in _combine_llm_outputs
    overall_token_usage[k] += v
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'float'
```

### Description

The merge loop in `ChatGroq._combine_llm_outputs` (`libs/partners/groq/langchain_groq/chat_models.py:829`) has three defects, all shown in the repro above:

**1. In-place mutation of caller data.** The first occurrence of a nested usage dict is stored by reference (`overall_token_usage[k] = v`), and merging the next output then does `overall_token_usage[k][nested_k] += nested_v` — mutating the first response's own `token_usage` dict. This is user-visible: in `BaseChatModel.generate` (`langchain_core/language_models/chat_models.py:1673-1685`) `_combine_llm_outputs` runs *before* the per-generation `llm_output` dicts are handed to `on_llm_end`, so callbacks and traces for the first generation report inflated nested counts (e.g. `cached_tokens` of generation 0 silently includes generation 1's).

**2. Inverted None-guard (silent data loss).** The loop reads `if k in overall_token_usage and v is not None: ... else: overall_token_usage[k] = v`, so a later `None` value falls into the `else` and *overwrites* an already-accumulated number. Groq really does return `None` here — `ChatGroq`'s own class docstring shows a live response with `'queue_time': None` in `token_usage`.

**3. None first, then a number → crash.** The same guard only checks the *new* value for None, so `None` stored first followed by a number hits `overall_token_usage[k] += v` → `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'float'` on a batched `generate()`.

(There's also a dead branch: `if k not in overall_token_usage` inside the path that requires `k in overall_token_usage`.)

Related: `langchain-mistralai` (#38482) and `langchain-fireworks` (#38648/#38646) have the naive `+=` version of this bug; groq attempted the nested handling but got the aliasing and None semantics wrong. `langchain-openai` has the reference implementation (`_update_token_usage`, `base.py:486`), which rebuilds nested dicts instead of mutating and skips None values.

I have a fix ready on a branch (`abcgco/langchain:fix-groq-combine-llm-outputs`): a recursive `_update_token_usage` following the `langchain-openai` pattern but extended to accept floats (Groq reports float timings such as `queue_time` / `prompt_time`, which the openai int-only version would reject), plus a `None` skip. Includes parametrized unit tests for the None/float cases and an input-immutability regression test; `make format lint test` green in `libs/partners/groq` (62 passed). Per the workflow I'll open the PR once assigned — could a maintainer assign this to me?

title: Fireworks LLM: async _acall error messages show a bound-method repr instead of the API response body (missing await)
body:
### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain-fireworks (the `Fireworks` completions LLM)

### Description

`Fireworks._acall` (the async path in `langchain_fireworks/llms.py`) builds its HTTP error messages with `{response.text}`. On an `aiohttp.ClientResponse`, `.text` is a **coroutine method**, not a property — unlike a `requests.Response`, where `.text` *is* a property. Because it is never awaited, the f-string interpolates the bound method's `repr()` instead of the response body.

So whenever the Fireworks API returns a 4xx/5xx during an **async** call (`ainvoke` / `agenerate`), the raised error hides the real reason and shows `<bound method ClientResponse.text ...>`. The **sync** path (`_call`, which uses `requests`) is correct. Notably the async method already correctly translated `requests`' `.status_code` to aiohttp's `.status`, but missed the analogous `.text` property-vs-coroutine difference — so this looks like an oversight rather than intent.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

The mismatch is deterministic and reproducible offline by mocking the aiohttp session to return a 4xx:
```python
import asyncio
from unittest.mock import patch

from langchain_fireworks import Fireworks


class _Resp:
    status = 400

    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *a):
        return False

    async def text(self):
        return "model does not exist"


class _Session:
    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *a):
        return False

    def post(self, *a, **k):
        return _Resp()


async def main():
    llm = Fireworks(model="foo", api_key="dummy")
    with patch("langchain_fireworks.llms.ClientSession", return_value=_Session()):
        await llm._acall("hi")


asyncio.run(main())
```

Real-world trigger: any `await Fireworks(...).ainvoke("...")` / `agenerate(...)` where Fireworks rejects the request (bad model name, invalid params, rate limit, server error).

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
ValueError: Fireworks received an invalid payload: <bound method _Resp.text of <__main__._Resp object at 0x...>>
```

Expected: the message should contain the actual API error body (here, `model does not exist`).

### Root cause / proposed fix

In `_acall`, the two error branches must `await` the body:
```python
if response.status >= 400:
    error_text = await response.text()
    msg = f"Fireworks received an invalid payload: {error_text}"
    raise ValueError(msg)
if response.status != 200:
    error_text = await response.text()
    msg = (
        f"Fireworks returned an unexpected response with status "
        f"{response.status}: {error_text}"
    )
    raise Exception(msg)
```

I have this fix plus a unit test ready (the test fails on current `master` — showing the `<bound method ...>` message — and passes with the fix; `libs/partners/fireworks` unit tests and `ruff` are green). Could a maintainer assign this to me so I can open the PR? I'll hold off until then per the contributor guidelines.

### System Info

`langchain-fireworks` on current `master`; `aiohttp` 3.x; Python 3.12. The sync `_call` path is unaffected.

Related Issues / PRs

- https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/35543 (fix on BaseChatOpenAI._create_chat_result, which missed the Azure override)

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
import warnings
from typing import Literal

import openai
from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr

from langchain_openai import AzureChatOpenAI


class ModelOutput(BaseModel):
    output: str


class MockParsedMessage(openai.BaseModel):
    role: Literal["assistant"] = "assistant"
    content: str = '{"output": "Paris"}'
    parsed: None = None
    refusal: str | None = None


class MockChoice(openai.BaseModel):
    index: int = 0
    finish_reason: Literal["stop"] = "stop"
    message: MockParsedMessage


class MockChatCompletion(openai.BaseModel):
    id: str = "chatcmpl-1"
    object: str = "chat.completion"
    created: int = 0
    model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
    choices: list[MockChoice]
    usage: dict[str, int] | None = None


parsed_response = ModelOutput(output="Paris")
response = MockChatCompletion.model_construct(
    choices=[
        MockChoice.model_construct(
            message=MockParsedMessage.model_construct(parsed=parsed_response)
        )
    ],
    usage={"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2},
)

llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
    azure_deployment="gpt-4o-mini",
    api_version="2024-10-01-preview",
    azure_endpoint="https://example.openai.azure.com",
    api_key=SecretStr("test"),
)

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    llm._create_chat_result(response)

print(f"# warnings: {len(caught)}")
for w in caught:
    print(w.category.__name__, str(w.message))
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
# warnings: 1
UserWarning Pydantic serializer warnings:
  PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue(Expected `none` - serialized value may not be as expected [field_name='parsed', input_value=ModelOutput(output='Paris'), input_type=ModelOutput])
```

### Description

https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/35543 added exclude={"choices": {"__all__": {"message": {"parsed"}}}} to BaseChatOpenAI._create_chat_result's response.model_dump() call to suppress PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warnings on structured-output responses.

AzureChatOpenAI._create_chat_result overrides the base method (to inspect Azure-specific content-filter metadata) and runs a second response.model_dump() on the same response without the same exclusion. Every Azure with_structured_output call therefore still emits the warning on this second dump. In our deployment these warnings show up on every chat-completion call that uses structured output and get ingested by log collectors at ERROR severity from stderr, drowning out real errors.

The fix is to mirror the same exclude into the Azure override..

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
# Problem 1: PIIMatch is NOT exported from the public package.
# The docs tell users to write a custom detector returning PIIMatch-shaped
# dicts, but the type itself cannot be imported publicly:
from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMatch
# ImportError: cannot import name 'PIIMatch'
# from 'langchain.agents.middleware'

# The only working import is from the private, underscore-prefixed module:
from langchain.agents.middleware._redaction import PIIMatch  # private API

# Problem 2: The official docs example for custom detectors returns dicts
# with "text"/"start"/"end", but the real PIIMatch TypedDict uses
# "type"/"value"/"start"/"end" (see _redaction.py below).
import re

def detect_ssn(content: str) -> list[PIIMatch]:
    """Custom detector following the docs example at
    https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/built-in
    """
    matches = []
    for match in re.finditer(r"\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}", content):
        ssn = match.group(0)
        matches.append({
            "text": ssn,            # docs say "text"  -> should be "value"
            "start": match.start(),
            "end": match.end(),
            # "type" field is missing, but PIIMatch requires it
        })
    return matches

# Source definition (libs/langchain/langchain/agents/middleware/_redaction.py):
# class PIIMatch(TypedDict):
#     type: str
#     value: str
#     start: int
#     end: int

# Built-in detectors confirm the real shape, e.g. detect_email:
#   PIIMatch(type="email", value=match.group(), start=..., end=...)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
# --- Problem 1: runtime ImportError ---
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'PIIMatch' from 'langchain.agents.middleware'

# --- Problem 2: type-checker error (Pyrefly) when following the docs example ---
Argument `(content: str) -> list[dict[str, int | str]]` is not assignable to
parameter `detector` with type `((str) -> list[PIIMatch]) | str | None` in
function `langchain.agents.middleware.pii.PIIMiddleware.__init__`
Pyrefly(bad-argument-type)

Field `text` is present in `<anonymous>` and absent in `PIIMatch`
Field `type` is required in `PIIMatch` but missing
```

### Description

Two issues with PIIMiddleware custom detectors:

1. PIIMatch (the return type required by the `detector` callable) is not
   exported from the public `langchain.agents.middleware` package, even though
   `pii.py` lists it in its own `__all__`. The package `__init__.py` only
   re-exports PIIDetectionError and PIIMiddleware. Since custom detectors are
   a documented public feature, users must import PIIMatch from the private
   `_redaction` module, which is not intended public API.

   Expected: `from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMatch` should work.

2. The custom-detector example on the docs page
   (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/built-in,
   "Custom PII types" -> "Method 3") returns dicts with "text"/"start"/"end",
   but the actual PIIMatch TypedDict uses "type"/"value"/"start"/"end".
   Following the docs as-is causes type-checker errors and, at runtime,
   redaction strategies cannot find the matched `value`.

   Expected: the docs example should use "type"/"value"/"start"/"end".

Both issues are present in 1.2.12 and still present in the latest 1.3.11.

title: PIIMiddleware: PIIMatch not exported from public package, and docs use wrong field names for custom detectors
body:
## Summary

When writing a **custom detector function** for `PIIMiddleware` (a documented public feature), there are two problems that make it unusable without reaching into private internals:

1. `PIIMatch` (the return type required by the `detector` callable) is **not exported** from the public `langchain.agents.middleware` package.
2. The **official documentation example** for custom detectors uses field names (`text`/`start`/`end`) that do **not match** the actual `PIIMatch` TypedDict (`type`/`value`/`start`/`end`).

## Problem 1 — `PIIMatch` is not publicly exported

`pii.py` lists `PIIMatch` in its own `__all__`:

`libs/langchain/langchain/agents/middleware/pii.py````python
__all__ = [
    "PIIDetectionError",
    "PIIMatch",
    "PIIMiddleware",
    "detect_credit_card",
    "detect_email",
    "detect_ip",
    "detect_mac_address",
    "detect_url",
]
```

…but the package `__init__.py` only re-exports `PIIDetectionError` and `PIIMiddleware`:

`libs/langchain/langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py````python
from langchain.agents.middleware.pii import PIIDetectionError, PIIMiddleware
# ...
__all__ = [
    # ...
    "PIIDetectionError",
    "PIIMiddleware",
    # (no PIIMatch)
]
```

The `detector` parameter type is `Callable[[str], list[PIIMatch]] | str | None` (`pii.py`), and the docs explicitly tell users to write a custom function returning `PIIMatch`-shaped dicts. So anyone writing a custom detector needs the `PIIMatch` type, but the only working import is from the underscore-prefixed private module:
```python
from langchain.agents.middleware._redaction import PIIMatch  # private API
```

### Expected

`PIIMatch` should be importable from the public package:
```python
from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMatch
```

## Problem 2 — Documentation example uses wrong field names

The custom-detector example on https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/built-in (under "Custom PII types" → "Method 3: Custom detector function") returns dicts with `text` / `start` / `end`:
```python
def detect_ssn(content: str) -> list[dict[str, str | int]]:
    """Detect SSN with validation.

    Returns a list of dictionaries with '"text"', '"start"', and '"end"' keys.
    """
    import re
    matches = []
    pattern = r"\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}"
    for match in re.finditer(pattern, content):
        ssn = match.group(0)
        first_three = int(ssn[:3])
        if first_three not in [0, 666] and not (900 <= first_three <= 999):
            matches.append({
                "text": ssn,
                "start": match.start(),
                "end": match.end(),
            })
    return matches
```

The "Custom detector function signature" block on the same page also says:
```python
def detector(content: str) -> list[dict[str, str | int]]:
    return [
        {"text": "matched_text", "start": 0, "end": 12},
    ]
```

However, the actual `PIIMatch` TypedDict in the source uses **`type` / `value` / `start` / `end`** (no `text` field, and `value` instead of `text`):

`libs/langchain/langchain/agents/middleware/_redaction.py````python
class PIIMatch(TypedDict):
    """Represents an individual match of sensitive data."""

    type: str
    value: str
    start: int
    end: int
```

The built-in detectors confirm this — e.g. `detect_email`:
```python
return [
    PIIMatch(
        type="email",
        value=match.group(),
        start=match.start(),
        end=match.end(),
    )
    for match in re.finditer(pattern, content)
]
```

### Impact

Following the documentation example as-is:

- Produces dicts with a `text` key and no `type` key, which do not conform to `PIIMatch`.
- Type checkers (Pyrefly/mypy) flag the detector callable as not assignable to `Callable[[str], list[PIIMatch]]`.
- At runtime the `value` field is missing, so redaction strategies that operate on the matched `value` do not behave as intended.

### Expected

The docs example should return `PIIMatch`-conformant dicts:
```python
def detect_ssn(content: str) -> list[PIIMatch]:
    matches = []
    pattern = r"\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}"
    for match in re.finditer(pattern, content):
        ssn = match.group(0)
        first_three = int(ssn[:3])
        if first_three not in [0, 666] and not (900 <= first_three <= 999):
            matches.append({
                "type": "ssn",
                "value": ssn,
                "start": match.start(),
                "end": match.end(),
            })
    return matches
```

(The docs source lives in the `langchain-ai/docs` repo at `src/oss/langchain/middleware/built-in.mdx` — happy to open a PR there as well if that is preferred.)

## Environment

- `langchain` version: 1.2.12 (also reproduced on **1.3.11**, latest at time of writing — both issues still present)
- Python 3.13

## Suggested fix

1. Add `PIIMatch` to the re-exports and `__all__` of `libs/langchain/langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py`.
2. Update the custom-detector example on the docs page to use `type`/`value`/`start`/`end` (and ideally annotate the return type as `list[PIIMatch]` once Problem 1 is fixed).

Happy to open a PR for either/both if maintainers indicate the preferred repo. Thanks!

title: Structured output with a raw JSON-schema dict is never validated, making ToolStrategy's handle_errors retry unreachable for dict schemas
body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain

### Related Issues / PRs

Related but distinct: #36349 (model returns plain text instead of calling the structured-output tool — a different failure mode). No existing issue covers the validation skip below.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
"""Repro: ToolStrategy with a raw JSON schema dict skips ALL output validation.

Tested on langchain 1.3.11 / langchain-core 1.4.8 / pydantic 2.13.4 (clean venv, `pip install langchain`).
"""

from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
from typing import Any

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.structured_output import ToolStrategy
from langchain_core.language_models.fake_chat_models import GenericFakeChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_core.runnables import Runnable
from pydantic import BaseModel


class ScriptedToolCallingModel(GenericFakeChatModel):
    """Fake chat model that accepts tool binding and replays scripted messages."""

    def bind_tools(self, tools: Sequence[Any], **kwargs: Any) -> Runnable:
        del tools, kwargs
        return self


REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA = {
    "title": "Report",
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "summary": {"type": "string"},
        "key_findings": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"finding": {"type": "string"}},
            },
        },
    },
    "required": ["summary", "key_findings"],
}

# The model calls the structured-output tool with key_findings as the STRING "[]"
# even though the schema requires an ARRAY of objects.
BAD_ARGS = {"summary": "All good.", "key_findings": "[]"}
# A corrected call, only ever reached if the agent validates and retries.
GOOD_ARGS = {"summary": "All good.", "key_findings": [{"finding": "ok"}]}


def scripted_model() -> ScriptedToolCallingModel:
    messages: Iterator[AIMessage] = iter(
        [
            AIMessage(
                content="",
                tool_calls=[{"name": "Report", "args": BAD_ARGS, "id": "call_1", "type": "tool_call"}],
            ),
            AIMessage(
                content="",
                tool_calls=[{"name": "Report", "args": GOOD_ARGS, "id": "call_2", "type": "tool_call"}],
            ),
        ]
    )
    return ScriptedToolCallingModel(messages=messages)


print("=== 1. response_format = ToolStrategy(<raw JSON schema dict>) ===")
agent = create_agent(
    model=scripted_model(),
    tools=[],
    response_format=ToolStrategy(REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA),
)
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [("user", "Write a report")]})
sr = result["structured_response"]
print("structured_response:", sr)
print("type of key_findings:", type(sr["key_findings"]).__name__)
print("model turns taken:", sum(isinstance(m, AIMessage) for m in result["messages"]))


print()
print("=== 2. Same scripted bad args, response_format = ToolStrategy(<Pydantic model>) ===")


class Report(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    key_findings: list[dict]


agent = create_agent(
    model=scripted_model(),
    tools=[],
    response_format=ToolStrategy(Report),
)
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [("user", "Write a report")]})
sr = result["structured_response"]
print("structured_response:", sr)
print("type of key_findings:", type(sr.key_findings).__name__)
print("model turns taken:", sum(isinstance(m, AIMessage) for m in result["messages"]))
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

No exception is raised — that is the bug (the invalid output is returned silently). Actual program output:
```shell
=== 1. response_format = ToolStrategy(<raw JSON schema dict>) ===
structured_response: {'summary': 'All good.', 'key_findings': '[]'}
type of key_findings: str
model turns taken: 1

=== 2. Same scripted bad args, response_format = ToolStrategy(<Pydantic model>) ===
structured_response: summary='All good.' key_findings=[{'finding': 'ok'}]
type of key_findings: list
model turns taken: 2
```

### Description

When `response_format` carries a **raw JSON schema dict**, the agent never validates the model's structured output against it: `_parse_with_schema` (`langchain/agents/structured_output.py`, lines 94-96) early-returns the data for `schema_kind == "json_schema"` ("Raw JSON schema has no corresponding Python type to instantiate"). Because `OutputToolBinding.parse` therefore can never raise for dict schemas, the `StructuredOutputValidationError` handling in `factory.py`'s `_handle_model_output` — the machinery behind `ToolStrategy.handle_errors` (error `ToolMessage` + retry) — is structurally unreachable for exactly this schema kind. The same skip also applies on the `ProviderStrategy` parse path (`ProviderStrategyBinding.parse` funnels through the same function), where only JSON-decode failures are caught client-side.

In the repro, case 1 shows a scripted model returning `key_findings` as the **string** `"[]"` where the schema requires an **array of objects**: the agent returns it as `structured_response` in one turn — no error, no retry. Case 2 shows the identical bad tool call against a Pydantic-class schema: validation raises, `handle_errors=True` sends the error back to the model, and the second (corrected) scripted call is used. The behavioral contract should not depend on how the same schema is expressed.

Expected: dict-schema outputs are validated against the JSON schema (e.g. via `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator`), so schema-violating output raises inside `parse()` and the existing `handle_errors` retry machinery fires exactly as it does for Pydantic/dataclass/TypedDict schemas. If a validation dependency is unwanted, an explicit documented statement that dict schemas are never validated (and that `handle_errors` is inert for them) would at least make the limitation discoverable — `ToolStrategy.handle_errors` documents catching validation errors with no dict-schema carve-out, and `OutputToolBinding.parse` documents `Raises: ValueError: If parsing fails`.

This matters in practice because dict schemas are the only option when the schema arrives dynamically (built from configuration or another runtime), and weaker models do emit degenerate structured output (placeholder strings where arrays belong) that currently sails through unvalidated.

The skip is unchanged on current `master` (`libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/structured_output.py`, same lines).

title: _resolve_schemas processes a repeated state schema at its FIRST position, so the explicit state_schema can lose field conflicts to middleware
body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain

### Related Issues / PRs

PR #37223 (merged 2026-05-06) introduced both the documented contract and the bug: its regression test `test_last_schema_wins_for_conflicting_field` covers three distinct schema types, but never a duplicated one.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
from typing import Annotated, NotRequired

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware, AgentState
from langchain_core.language_models.fake_chat_models import GenericFakeChatModel


def base_reducer(left: int, right: int) -> int:
    return right


def middleware_reducer(left: int, right: int) -> int:
    return left + right


class MyState(AgentState):
    """The caller's explicit state_schema."""

    score: NotRequired[Annotated[int, base_reducer]]


class OtherState(AgentState):
    """A middleware schema that re-annotates the same field with a different reducer."""

    score: NotRequired[Annotated[int, middleware_reducer]]


class UsesBaseStateMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):
    """Middleware written against the agent's own state type (common pattern)."""

    state_schema = MyState


class ConflictingMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):
    state_schema = OtherState


model = GenericFakeChatModel(messages=iter([]))

agent1 = create_agent(
    model=model,
    middleware=[UsesBaseStateMiddleware(), ConflictingMiddleware()],
    state_schema=MyState,
)
print("case 1 [UsesBaseState, Conflicting]:", agent1.channels["score"].operator.__name__)
print("  expected: base_reducer (base state_schema is appended last, so it must win)")

# Same agent, only the middleware order is swapped -- the winner flips.
agent2 = create_agent(
    model=model,
    middleware=[ConflictingMiddleware(), UsesBaseStateMiddleware()],
    state_schema=MyState,
)
print("case 2 [Conflicting, UsesBaseState]:", agent2.channels["score"].operator.__name__)
print("  expected: base_reducer")
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

No exception is raised — the wrong reducer is silently installed. Actual output (langchain 1.3.11, langchain-core 1.4.8, Python 3.12, no network — the fake model is never invoked):
```shell
case 1 [UsesBaseState, Conflicting]: middleware_reducer
  expected: base_reducer (base state_schema is appended last, so it must win)
case 2 [Conflicting, UsesBaseState]: base_reducer
  expected: base_reducer
```

### Description

`_resolve_schemas` (`langchain/agents/factory.py`) documents: "a type that appears more than once is processed at its last position", and its call site appends the base schema last precisely so it wins field conflicts ("base_state last so it wins any field conflict"). The implementation cannot deliver that: `schema_hints = {schema: _get_schema_type_hints(schema) for schema in schemas}` relies on dict semantics, which keep the FIRST insertion position of a duplicated key (re-inserting only refreshes the value, which is identical anyway). So `[Base, Other, Base]` collapses to `[Base, Other]`, and the later merge (last entry wins) hands the conflict to `Other` — the opposite of the documented semantics.

The practical trigger is common: a middleware authored against the application's own state type (`state_schema = MyState` on the middleware, `state_schema=MyState` on `create_agent`). As soon as any later middleware re-annotates a shared field, the explicit base schema silently loses — and as the repro shows, which reducer wins now depends on middleware order, which the docstring says cannot happen. (Default middleware do not mask the issue: `AgentMiddleware.state_schema` defaults to a distinct type, so the duplication only arises when the caller introduces it — exactly the case above.)

Expected: both cases print `base_reducer`.

Suggested fix: dedupe keeping the LAST occurrence before building the hints dict, e.g.
```python
schemas = list(reversed(dict.fromkeys(reversed(schemas))))
```

followed by the existing comprehension — verified locally that with this change both middleware orders resolve `score` to `base_reducer`. A regression test extending `test_last_schema_wins_for_conflicting_field` with a duplicated type (e.g. `_resolve_schemas([LastState, MiddleState, LastState])` resolving the shared field to `LastState`'s annotation) would pin the contract.

The comprehension and docstring are unchanged on current `master` (`libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/factory.py`, commit 6e51a7e).

title: langchain-deepseek: Missing reasoning_content passback in _get_request_payload causes 400 error on multi-turn agent calls
body:
### Description

When using `langchain-deepseek` with DeepSeek models that support thinking mode (e.g., `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-r1`), calling `agent.invoke()` fails on the second internal LLM call with a 400 error.

DeepSeek API requires that when an assistant message with `reasoning_content` is sent back to the API in a subsequent request, the `reasoning_content` field must be preserved in the message. However, `ChatDeepSeek._get_request_payload()` does not pass through `reasoning_content` from the original `AIMessage.additional_kwargs` to the API payload, causing the request to be rejected.

### Error Message
```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400
{'error': {'message': 'The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.', 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': None, 'code': 'invalid_request_error'}}
```

### Full Traceback
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test_agent.py", line 17, in <module>
    res = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]})
  File ".../langgraph/pregel/main.py", line 3365, in invoke
    for chunk in self.stream(...)
  ...
  File ".../langchain_deepseek/chat_models.py", line 356, in _generate
    return super()._generate(...)
  File ".../langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py", line 1653, in _generate
    _handle_openai_bad_request(e)
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.'}}
```

### Reproduction Code

> This code is for testing purposes only.
```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

@tool(description="query weather")
def get_weather() -> str:
    return "sunny"

model = init_chat_model(model="deepseek-v4-flash")

agent = create_agent(
    model=model,
    tools=[get_weather],
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant.",
)

res = agent.invoke({
    "messages": [
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather tomorrow?"},
    ]
})

for msg in res["messages"]:
    print(type(msg).__name__, msg.content)
```

### Root Cause

The issue is in `ChatDeepSeek._get_request_payload()`. Here's the data flow:

1. **First LLM call**: DeepSeek returns an assistant message with `reasoning_content` + `tool_calls`
2. `_create_chat_result()` correctly extracts `reasoning_content` and stores it in `AIMessage.additional_kwargs["reasoning_content"]`
3. **Second LLM call**: `BaseChatOpenAI._get_request_payload()` calls `_convert_message_to_dict()` to serialize the previous assistant message
4. `_convert_message_to_dict()` does **not** merge `additional_kwargs` into the top-level dict — it only extracts standard OpenAI fields (`content`, `role`, `tool_calls`)
5. The resulting API payload is missing `reasoning_content`, causing DeepSeek API to return a 400 error

### Fix

The `_get_request_payload` method needs to retrieve the original `AIMessage` objects and pass through `reasoning_content` from `additional_kwargs` to the API payload.

Patch applied to `_get_request_payload` in `libs/partners/deepseek/langchain_deepseek/chat_models.py`:
```python
def _get_request_payload(
    self,
    input_: LanguageModelInput,
    *,
    stop: list[str] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> dict:
    payload = super()._get_request_payload(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)

    # Get original messages to preserve reasoning_content from assistant messages.
    # DeepSeek requires reasoning_content from previous responses to be passed
    # back in subsequent requests, but _convert_message_to_dict drops it.
    messages = self._convert_input(input_).to_messages()

    for i, message in enumerate(payload["messages"]):
        if message["role"] == "assistant":
            if isinstance(message.get("content"), list):
                text_parts = [
                    block.get("text", "")
                    for block in message["content"]
                    if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text"
                ]
                message["content"] = "".join(text_parts) if text_parts else ""

            # Pass through reasoning_content from original AIMessage
            if i < len(messages) and isinstance(messages[i], AIMessage):
                reasoning = messages[i].additional_kwargs.get(
                    "reasoning_content"
                )
                if reasoning is not None:
                    message["reasoning_content"] = reasoning

        elif message["role"] == "tool" and isinstance(message["content"], list):
            message["content"] = json.dumps(message["content"])
    return payload
```

### Environment

- `langchain-deepseek`: 1.0.1
- Model: `deepseek-v4-flash` (also affects `deepseek-r1`)
- OS: Windows 11

### Background

I'm a college student from Tianjin, China, currently learning the LangChain framework. I encountered this issue while building a simple agent for testing purposes.

title: MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter splits nested custom headers into separate chunks when strip_headers=False
body:
### Related Issues / PRs
- Related to #31887 (custom header pattern support)

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)```python
from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter

splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter(
    headers_to_split_on=[("**", "Header 1"), ("***", "Header 2")],
    custom_header_patterns={"**": 1, "***": 2},
    strip_headers=False,
)

for doc in splitter.split_text("**H1**\n***H2***\nbody\n"):
    print(repr(doc.page_content), doc.metadata)
```

Actual output:```python
'**H1**' {'Header 1': 'H1'}
'***H2***\nbody' {'Header 1': 'H1', 'Header 2': 'H2'}
```

Comparable standard-header case:```python
splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter(
    headers_to_split_on=[("#", "Header 1"), ("##", "Header 2")],
    strip_headers=False,
)

for doc in splitter.split_text("# H1\n## H2\nbody\n"):
    print(repr(doc.page_content), doc.metadata)
```

Output:```python
'# H1  \n## H2\nbody' {'Header 1': 'H1', 'Header 2': 'H2'}
```

### Description
`MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter` handles `custom_header_patterns` during header parsing, but the preserve-headers aggregation path still appears to special-case only `#`-style headers.

When `strip_headers=False`, nested standard Markdown headers are merged into a single chunk if they are immediately followed by a deeper header. The equivalent nested custom headers are split into two chunks instead, leaving the parent header as a header-only chunk.

I would expect custom headers to follow the same aggregation semantics as standard headers here, since both are already treated as tracked headers during parsing.

The behavior seems to come from `aggregate_lines_to_chunks()`, where the preserve-headers merge branch checks whether the previous chunk's last line starts with `#` before merging. That works for standard headers but not for custom header patterns like `**Header**`.

This looks like a small `langchain-text-splitters`-only regression/follow-up bug rather than a feature request. If this scope looks good, I can send a focused regression-test + fix PR.

### System Info
- Reproduced against `langchain-ai/langchain` `master` on July 7, 2026.
- Area: `langchain-text-splitters`
- Platform used for reproduction: macOS

### Related Issues / PRs

The first time the concept of `Reducer` is introduced in the documentation is lacking in context, in particular as regards to the implementation of left-hand-side and right-hand-side arguments, `left` and right`, representing the state before and after an update was applied. 

I propose that an amendment be made to the documentation to more clearly explain what a reducer is and how it functions the first time this concept is introduced. In particular, a discussion about the `left` and `right` arguments needs to be included in the definition of the reducer function as implemented in LangChain. 

From the documentation, there is a section titled "Default reducer", but there is no other section title describing the "non-default" reducer below it. This needs to change. Further, there is no discussion about the `left` and `right` arguments which needs to be mentioned right when the concept of reducer is explained, and not later on in other sections of the documentation such as Using the Graph API. 

So I propose a change to something along the lines of: 
1. Include a clear title that names and explains the "non-default" reducer (could be named "Custom reducer" for example). 
2. Include a discussion about the left and right hand arguments, for example as below, which enriches the meaning of a reducer: 

**Understanding Reducer Arguments**
In LangGraph, a reducer is a function responsible for determining how a new update (the right argument) should be merged into the existing state (the left argument).

When a node returns an update for a state channel, LangGraph invokes the associated reducer with two arguments:

left: Represents the current value of the state channel in the checkpoint. This is the "base" or "existing" data before the new update is applied.
right: Represents the new value(s) or update(s) provided by the node.
The reducer's purpose is to return a new value that represents the combined result of left and right. This returned value is then saved as the new state in the next checkpoint.

**Design Pattern**
For simple replacement: If you do not define a reducer, LangGraph defaults to replacing the entire state with the new value, effectively ignoring left and returning right.

For accumulation: To preserve existing data (e.g., appending to a list or merging a dictionary), define a function that explicitly combines left and right.```
def update_preferences(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
    # Merge existing preferences (left) with new updates (right)
    return {**left, **right}
```
By ensuring your reducer is a pure function that returns the combined state of left and right, you guarantee consistent, predictable state management during graph execution and time-travel replays.

P.S. This is not a bug, but I filed this under a bug because there is not separate template for proposing changes to the documentation (the closest one is Feature request, but that is not fitting either). I propose that a separate template be generated to allow for generating issues related to the documentation, as an issue is required to open a PR to make changes to the documentation as described in the guidelines.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)
```python
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from langchain.agents.middleware._execution import HostExecutionPolicy
from langchain.agents.middleware.shell_tool import ShellSession


def main() -> None:
    policy = HostExecutionPolicy(
        create_process_group=False,
        command_timeout=0.1,
        termination_timeout=0.05,
    )

    session = ShellSession(
        workspace=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lc-shell-repro-")),
        policy=policy,
        command=("/bin/bash",),
        environment={},
    )

    kill_calls: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    original_killpg = os.killpg
    try:
        # Safety: capture killpg call instead of actually killing the process group.
        os.killpg = lambda pgid, sig: kill_calls.append((pgid, sig))  # type: ignore[assignment]

        session.start()
        _ = session.execute("sleep 5", timeout=policy.command_timeout)

        current_pgid = os.getpgrp()
        child_pgid = os.getpgid(session._process.pid) if session._process else None

        print("create_process_group:", policy.create_process_group)
        print("current_pgid:", current_pgid)
        print("child_pgid:", child_pgid)
        print("kill_calls:", kill_calls)

        if not kill_calls:
            raise RuntimeError("Expected _kill_process to call os.killpg at least once.")
        if kill_calls[0][0] != current_pgid:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Expected killpg target process group to match caller process group."
            )
    finally:
        os.killpg = original_killpg  # type: ignore[assignment]
        session.stop(0.2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)
```shell
No Python exception is required to observe the bug. The bug is behavioral and visible from the printed output.

Example output:
create_process_group: False
current_pgid: 249430
child_pgid: 249430
kill_calls: [(249430, 9)]
```

### Description

- I am using ShellToolMiddleware internals with HostExecutionPolicy(create_process_group=False).
- I expect timeout cleanup to terminate only the child shell process.
- Instead, _kill_process uses process-group kill unconditionally via os.killpg(os.getpgid(child_pid), SIGKILL).
- When create_process_group=False, the child shares the caller process group, so the kill target can include the caller and sibling processes.

title: `ChatOpenRouter` silently swallows `default_headers`
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version.
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example.

### Package

`langchain-openrouter`

### Bug summary

`ChatOpenRouter` does not declare a `default_headers` field and provides no way to inject arbitrary HTTP headers through its public API. Worse, attempting to pass `default_headers={...}` silently corrupts the value: the `build_extra` validator (mode="before") strips the unrecognized field into `model_kwargs` with a misleading warning, after which the supposed "headers" end up serialized into the request **body** instead of as HTTP headers.

This blocks any feature that depends on per-request HTTP header injection. The motivating case for me is xAI's `x-grok-conv-id` header, which routes consecutive requests with the same value to the same upstream xAI server so its prompt cache stays warm. Empirically this is worth a +45.9pp cache hit rate improvement on grok-4.1-fast (75.2% with header vs 29.3% without, measured over 12 interleaved request pairs against `api.x.ai`). With the bug, there's no way to deliver that header through `ChatOpenRouter` even when going BYOK to xAI through OpenRouter.

### Reproducer
```python
from langchain_openrouter import ChatOpenRouter

llm = ChatOpenRouter(
    model=\"x-ai/grok-4.1-fast\",
    default_headers={\"x-grok-conv-id\": \"session-abc-123\"},
)
# Triggers a UserWarning:
#   WARNING! default_headers is not default parameter.
#   default_headers was transferred to model_kwargs.
#   Please confirm that default_headers is what you intended.
#
# And the header never reaches httpx — inspect the underlying client:
sdk_cfg = llm.client.sdk_configuration
print(dict(sdk_cfg.async_client.headers))
# {'accept': '*/*', ..., 'http-referer': '...', 'x-title': '...'}
# 'x-grok-conv-id' is missing entirely.
```

### Expected behavior

`ChatOpenRouter(default_headers={...})` should accept the field cleanly and forward those headers on every request, the same way `ChatOpenAI` and other OpenAI-compat chat models do via `default_headers`.

### Actual behavior

The field is silently absorbed into `model_kwargs`, the misleading warning is shown, and the header value is serialized as a body field on every request (where it does nothing). Inspection of the underlying httpx client shows the header is never set.

### Root cause

`ChatOpenRouter` inherits from `BaseChatModel` (not `BaseChatOpenAI`), so it doesn't get OpenAI-compat constructor fields like `default_headers` for free. Its `build_extra` validator (`langchain_openrouter/chat_models.py:297-325`) catches any kwarg not in the declared field set and shoves it into `model_kwargs`:
```python
@model_validator(mode=\"before\")
def build_extra(cls, values):
    all_required_field_names = get_pydantic_field_names(cls)
    extra = values.get(\"model_kwargs\", {})
    for field_name in list(values):
        if field_name not in all_required_field_names:
            warnings.warn(
                f\"WARNING! {field_name} is not default parameter. \"
                f\"{field_name} was transferred to model_kwargs...\"
            )
            extra[field_name] = values.pop(field_name)
    values[\"model_kwargs\"] = extra
    return values
```

So unless `default_headers` is a declared field, this validator quietly turns it into a body field. The only way to inject custom headers today is to pre-build an `openrouter.OpenRouter` SDK client with a custom `httpx.AsyncClient` and pass it via the `client` field — undocumented and brittle.

Notably, `_build_client` (`chat_models.py:339-359`) **already** uses the exact pattern needed: it pre-builds httpx clients with the app-attribution headers (`HTTP-Referer`, `X-Title`, `X-OpenRouter-Categories`). It just doesn't expose a generic `default_headers` field to merge into that same dict.

### Proposed fix

Add a `default_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None` field and merge it into the existing `extra_headers` dict in `_build_client`. ~3 lines of code plus a docstring. User-supplied headers should take precedence over built-in attribution headers if a key collides.

I have a branch with this fix plus four unit tests in `TestChatOpenRouterInstantiation` (verified to fail before the fix with the exact \"transferred to model_kwargs\" warning, and pass after, with `make format`/`make lint`/`make test` all green and 224/224 tests passing):

https://github.com/untilhamza/langchain/tree/fix/openrouter-default-headers

Happy to open a PR once assigned.

### System Info

- langchain-openrouter: master
- Python: 3.12
- OS: macOS

title: Bug: streaming tool call fires prematurely with empty args when SSE fragments arguments across chunks
body:
## Description

When upstream providers (e.g. OpenRouter, deepseek-v3.2) fragment tool call arguments across multiple SSE chunks, the first chunk arrives with `args=""` (empty string). `AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls` treats `args=""` and `args=None` identically — both resolve to `{}` — so the tool call is created immediately before the actual arguments have been received.

## Steps to reproduce
```python
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessageChunk

# Simulate first SSE chunk: tool call with empty args (still streaming)
chunk1 = AIMessageChunk(
    content="",
    tool_call_chunks=[{"name": "get_weather", "args": "", "id": "call_abc", "index": 0}]
)
# Bug: tool_calls is already populated after the first chunk
print(chunk1.tool_calls)  # [{'name': 'get_weather', 'args': {}, 'id': 'call_abc', 'type': 'tool_call'}]
# Expected: [] — arguments haven't arrived yet
```

## Root cause

In `libs/core/langchain_core/messages/ai.py`, `init_tool_calls` takes the `else` branch for both `args=None` and `args=""`, producing `args={}` in both cases. An empty string means the stream is still in progress; it should not produce a tool call yet.

## Impact

Agents using streaming with providers that fragment tool call arguments crash with `ValidationError: Field required` when the tool is invoked with `{}` before the real arguments arrive. Affects any agent using OpenRouter, deepseek-v3.2, or similar providers.

## Fix

Skip creating the tool call when `args_str == ""` and we are not at the last stream chunk. I have a fix ready — will open a PR linked to this issue.
